figures.finding: Bhutan's public money for film is a loan: in September 2024 the government set aside Nu 200 million under its Economic Stimulus Plan, including soft loans for film production.

value.allocation: proposed by the Film Association of Bhutan on script, cast and direction

sources.said: THIMPHU – In a bid to revive the country’s beleaguered film industry, the government has allocated Nu 200 million as part of its Economic Stimulus Plan (ESP). … The government’s intervention includes a soft loan component designed to stimulate production of films.

figures.finding: Bhutan was making about 30 films a year by 2010, before its first national film policy (2013), with no film school and no film development fund.

sources.said: Though film industry in Bhutan boomed within a short span of time, producing 30 films a year by 2010 yet without policy in place its growth lacked in the quality department. Much of the poor quality of films has been attributed to the challenges faced by the film industry such as lack of a film school and film development fund

figures.finding: Every film shot in Bhutan needs a permit from the media authority and pays a royalty of USD 10,000 for a film (USD 3,000 a TV documentary, USD 3,000 an episode for a TV series) plus a USD 2,000 refundable deposit, with no exemption; the royalties go to the Media Development Fund the authority administers.

value.fund: Media Development Fund (sub-fund of the Universal Service Fund)

figures.applies: Bhutan; Bhutan Filming Regulation, in force 22 March 2007 (later revisions not read).

sources.said: All filming royalty fees collected shall be retained and deposited into the Media Development Fund, a sub-fund created under the Universal Service Fund as per Section 57 of the Act, to be administered by the Authority. … This Regulation shall come into force from the 22nd Day of March 2007. … There shall be no exemption of the fee under any circumstances.
